title: From Cells to Survival: Hierarchical Analysis of Cell Inter-Relations in Multiplex Microscopy for Lung Cancer Prognosis
authors: Edgren Schüllerqvist, Olle; Baumann, Jens; Lindblad, Joakim; Nordling, Love et al.
summary: A hierarchical GNN models local cell interactions and tissue-level organization in multiplex microscopy, with cancer-stage fusion further improving lung cancer survival risk stratification.
takeaways: Integrating cancer stage (CS) as complementary information enhances performance.
Each cell in the graph is considered the same node type, while cell type information is included as node features.
They used data augmentation to improve robustness by generating four sets of subsample graphs per core with varying overlaps.

title: Spatial immunophenotyping of the tumour microenvironment in non-small cell lung cancer
authors: Max Backman, Carina Strell, Amanda Lindberg et al.
summary: A multiplexed fluorescence imaging study that spatially quantified 13 immune-cell subsets and their interactions in 359 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cases.
takeaways: Biological signals that contribute to anti-cancer immunity are crucially needed for better and more optimized clinical diagnostics and treatments.
Immune cells other than T cells have a stronger association with patient survival.
They used Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) for mutation analysis.

title: Proteina: Scaling Flow-based Protein Structure Generative Models
authors: Tomas Geffner, Kieran Didi, Zuobai Zhang et al.
summary: A scalable flow-matching model for protein backbone generation that combines a Transformer architecture with hierarchical fold-class conditioning and pairwise structural representations.
takeaways: Flow matching is combined with a scalable Transformer architecture for protein backbone generation.
The architecture uses sequence representation, sequence conditioning, and pair representation to model protein structure.
Hierarchical fold-class conditioning provides control over the generated protein structures.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Ricky T. Q. Chen, Yulia Rubanova, Jesse Bettencourt, David Duvenaud
summary: Introduces a new family of deep neural networks parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE), where network evaluation is computed using a numerical ODE solver, offering constant memory cost and continuous-depth modeling.
takeaways: Replaces traditional discrete layers with a continuous-depth transformation defined by an ODE.
Uses the adjoint sensitivity method to compute gradients with constant memory consumption regardless of network depth.
Enables continuous normalizing flows and naturally handles irregularly-sampled time-series data.
